releases: B1: coverage by registered month and partition label (every month listed, so a gap shows as 0); records with no anchor; records with no label; of PRO-V these are index record counts and nothing else
B2: counts by population code per cell, which reconcile to the record count
B3: counts by class per cell

B4: per cell and model: scored orders, fills, fills by kind, fills within 1 s and 2 s of t, fills by kind in the after-the-hour seconds and in the second and the third minute after the hour, fills in a batch that moves the market from OPEN to not OPEN, fills in the batch that turns the market in play, orders ended by the pull and by the lapse, and the fill rate; and the fill counts per model of each class that is not scored

B5: per cell and model: the sample SD of gross g at the BSP as written over filled orders and its symmetric ranges q95 - q05, q90 - q10 and q75 - q25, and none of them for a model that leaves fewer than statistics.min_values scored orders unfilled (flagged filled_is_all_placed); quantiles of the size shown at t ahead of the order (the pessimistic model's queue); per model the seconds to a fill as quantiles
B8: per cell of the each_active rule file: the runners of the markets whose market rows hold, by the code of their first failing runner row, and the runners ordered on
B9: per cell: orders placed, scored orders and pessimistic fills by the gap at t in CLASSIC ticks: 1-2, 3-5, 6-10, 11-20
There is no B6: close-v1's detectable effect describes a test, and none is run
blind_pass.rule: The blind look runs first, once, and gives only what releases lists. Both passes read the explore label alone (data.partitions). lab-Claude reads the look in daylight and writes its reading down before anything else runs. S0: stop and tell Yu if the receipt's input_sha256 is not the one close-v1's passes named. S1: stop and tell Yu if a code column does not add up to the records, classes do not add up to orders, any fill of kind trade_through or volume_at_price lies in the after-the-hour seconds, or, over the cells of one rule file under the pessimistic model, the trade_through fills in the second minute after the hour number 40 or more and are more than twice those in the third minute. S2: a cell is dropped when the markets with an order at its time (issued) are fewer than half of those at -1800 in the same rule file. S3: a cell is dropped when the pessimistic model has fewer than statistics.min_tested_values fills on statistics.min_tested_race_dates race dates; the explore pass enforces this by code and gives that cell's counts only. S4: when the cells at -3600, -7200 and -14400 of a rule file are all dropped, that rule file's early variants end there. S5: when every cell is dropped the explore pass is not run. No code enforces S0, S1, S2, S4 or S5: the written reading does, and a dropped cell's figures, if the explore pass prints them, are not read. If the explore pass runs, it runs once, on a later night, at the same code commit and backtest sources, and only with the blind receipt of this registration, split file and input; the runner refuses anything else, and refuses a second explore pass of this study. Nothing in this file or in the code may change between the two passes. A stop is not a reason for a second look. Of an outcome the blind look gives only statistics that a shift leaves as they are: the sample SD and the symmetric ranges.
withholds: every mean, median, raw quantile, sign, interval, test, label and selection of an outcome
any SD of net_closed or net_held: the kink at 0 leaks the location (inference)
the SD over unfilled orders, and the SD over all scored orders even where close-v1 let it stand in for a model's filled SD: either beside a filled SD bounds the size of the gap
any outcome statistic by gap, price or half-year
any per-market or per-runner row, market id or selection id

data.duplicates: A record of the registered tier is keyed by its market id alone; one id twice in that tier refuses the run (input:<archive sha256>:duplicate_market), so no market is decided or counted twice. Keep the PRO archive in its own data root. A record of another plan is coded plan_not_registered.
data.files: The runner reads the split file beside the studies/ folder that holds this registration, and the rule files in rules/ beside that folder; in the repository these are research/ and research/rules/. Each file's sha256 must equal the one named here. A name is a plain file name, never a path.
data.month: the UTC month of the first-published marketTime

partitions.rule: Every record gets the label of its race date from the split file (partition.Split.label). The race date is the Europe/London calendar date of the first-published off. read is explore_only: both passes of this study read the explore label alone. A record on any other label is coded partition_not_registered at every cell its history gates let through, from its index record alone, and its file is never opened; the runner refuses to open a file whose label is not read. PRO-V is named under the key test because the parser fixes that key and asks for a holdout label there; nothing is tested, and of PRO-V a pass gives index record counts and nothing else. Each pass's ledger line names PRO-D alone. Every pass parses every index line, and every index line holds BSP and results, so the split is kept by code paths and tests, not by separate files.

data.source: every archive ingested and indexed under one data root (archive.py, market_index.py), each market from its index record's primary member, replayed with the index's own fold, checked against the record at every decision time (replay.view_from_fold) and read on, message by message, to the last pull time of the cells that reached the book; nothing later is parsed, and no other source stands in

traded_volume.rule: As close-v1 (research/studies/close-v1.json, data.traded_volume.rule), folded by the same code (lp.TradedFold), with one change. PRO rc.trd counts backer's stake x 2, so a matched backer's stake of s shows as a rise of divisor x s; atb and atl sizes are backer's stake, with no divisor. Messages sharing a pt are one batch. A batch is open when the market status in force before its first message is OPEN. A rise counts as traded volume only in an open batch, only when that batch also carries an atb or atl entry at that price for that runner, and (the change: hour_rises is not_counted) only when the batch's pt does not lie in the first after_the_hour_s seconds after a whole UTC hour on a Monday to Friday. Some trd updates are currency restatements, sent a few seconds after each whole hour on those days (docs/lp-study.md); one that shares a batch with a ladder entry at its price would otherwise count as a trade, and an order that rests for hours meets several whole hours. A rise that is not counted is never counted later, so it fills nothing by trade_through or volume_at_price; quote_cross reads the ladder and is still judged in those seconds. A true trade in those seconds is lost with the restatements, so fills are understated, never overstated; an order placed exactly on a whole hour loses the first after_the_hour_s seconds of its trades. after_the_hour_s is a reading of a few seconds, not a measured bound; the diagnostics count trade fills in the second and the third minute after the hour to check it. The settlement-zeroing frame is counted and ignored.

decided_by: lab-Claude proposed this study on 2026-11-16, in its recommendation to Yu on liquidity provision, as offline work on data already held. It relies on Yu's standing word of 2026-11-12, as docs/research-loop.md records it under Who merges and who starts a pass: lab-Claude reads that word as yes to merging its own offline research pull requests after an independent review and to starting night passes. The reading is lab-Claude's, and Yu can correct it at any time. It covers no live order, no stake or other money number and no policy page. Yu chose none of the numbers here: the cells, the gates, the two switches and the closing lines are lab-Claude's, from a design of 2026-11-16 and two attacks on it. On 2026-11-16 Yu said yes when lab-Claude asked whether this file may say that the study, which asks only a LAY at early-price-v1's times and price ranges, was designed after the earlier results were read, and whether split file version 3 may carry its three sentences; that this yes covers these texts is lab-Claude's reading, and the record is in the lab's notes.

diagnostics.rule: Counts only, in both passes; they change no code, class or statistic, and one that shows a rule wrong leads to a fix, a new registration and a new blind look, put to Yu first. Per cell and model: fills within each of within_s seconds of t; fills by kind whose pt lies in the first data.traded_volume.after_the_hour_s seconds after a whole UTC hour on a Monday to Friday, which must number 0 here for trade_through and volume_at_price; fills by kind in the second and in the third minute after such an hour, which are alike if the first minute holds every restatement; fills in an open batch that left the market not OPEN; fills in the batch that turned the market in play; orders ended unfilled by the pull and by the lapse. Per order, over (t, pull time] and its runner (trd_counts): rises counted as trades; rises not counted, in an open batch outside the after-the-hour seconds, at a price that was the best back or best lay just before the batch; rises in a batch that was not open; rises left out in the after-the-hour seconds that the counting rule would otherwise have counted, which is what the switch removes. Per cell: orders placed in the after-the-hour seconds; orders placed, scored orders and pessimistic fills by the gap at t in CLASSIC ticks, in four ranges; scored orders with a batch in (t, pull time] that began with no market status; null values undefined, by reason; cells that passed a flag gate with no value for the flag at t. Per cell of the each_active rule file: the runners of the markets whose market rows hold, by the code of their first failing runner row, and the runners ordered on. Scored BSPs that are whole hundredths and those that are not.

exposure.fresh_on_test: Nothing is tested and no pass of this study opens a PRO-V file, so nothing here is fresh or spent on a test label. Not printed by any earlier study on any date of this year, as far as the repository's pages show: quotes, queues and fills more than 30 minutes before the off.

lines.close-v1: The same LAY on the favourite at 10, 5 and 2 minutes before the off, with a gap gate of 1 or 2 ticks, on both labels, with the lineage's one test on PRO-V. Per cell and label it released fill counts, mean scores against BSP and the gap between filled and unfilled orders, and half-year figures for every cell on PRO-D and for the primaries on PRO-V; they are on the lab and this study's designer knew them. This study's favourite rule file is that LAY file with earlier times, a row for a missing best lay and a wider gap gate (parent_sha256).
lines.early-price-v1: Last traded prices against BSP at these four times and in these two price ranges, on the BASIC files of 2023 and 2024. Its results are on the lab, and this study was designed after they were read. Another decade, and no quotes.
lines.lp-v1: On every date, at 10, 5 and 2 minutes before the off, lp-v1 rested a LAY at the best back price, behind the size shown, of the shortest-priced runner with a best back of 1.50 to 10.0 and a gap of 3 to 20 ticks, which is rarely the favourite, and released fill counts and, for those join legs at 10 minutes, how far the mid moved after a fill (docs/lp-study.md). So a resting LAY across a wide gap on a runner that is not the favourite is not new to this year; every time earlier than 10 minutes, and the order's own price scored against BSP, are. This study's gap gate was widened by someone who could know lp-v1's results.
lines.movement-v1: Taker NCLV of the favourite's best back by decision time on every date of this year, 30 minutes before the off included (docs/movement-study.md). So the level of the price the favourite order asks 30 minutes out was known on every date, PRO-V dates included.
lines.p0: The year counts as inspected from P0's first run (docs/movement-study.md). Its outcome metrics stay on the lab.
lines.p0-basic-2015-16: The BASIC files of the same races. This study reads the PRO files and no BASIC file.
lines.p0-basic-2023-25: Other years and another tier. A record of them is coded from the index alone and its file is never opened.
lines.suite-counts: Whole-year counts of in-play markets and of markets with a removal. Counts, not locations.

exposure.not_fresh_on_test: The 2015-16 PRO year is not fresh on any date. movement-v1, lp-v1 and close-v1 read these files on every date, PRO-V dates included, and close-v1 spent the close lineage's one test on PRO-V. The idea is not fresh either: this is close-v1's LAY at earlier times and on more runners, and this study was designed after the results of close-v1 and early-price-v1 had been read on the lab. So it is a description with its closing lines written first, not a test.
exposure.printed_with_every_label: Explore dates of 2015-16 only. That year is not fresh, the idea is the lineage close again, and nothing here is tested.

family.rule: Nothing is tested: no family, no p-value, no Holm step. alpha is 0.0 because this study spends none, and the ledger refuses a registered line that carries no alpha. m and method are kept because the parser asks for them; nothing reads them. The runner refuses the registered pass for this study id.

fill_models.rule: We do not know our place in the queue, so every order is judged three times; the models differ only in the queue. queue = queue_fraction (numerator, denominator) x the size shown at t at the order's price on its own side (a LAY rests on atb, a BACK on atl): optimistic is the front of the queue, central is behind half the size shown, pessimistic is behind all of it (lp-v1's join rule). A fill is judged when a pt batch is complete, for the batches after t up to and including the pull time. The first kind that holds, in the order of kinds: trade_through, the batch counts a rise at a price beyond the order's (below a LAY, above a BACK), whatever its size; quote_cross, the batch carried an image or a ladder key for the runner and the size then shown on the opposite side at or through the order's price (atl at or below a LAY, atb at or above a BACK) is at least the stake; volume_at_price, the counted volume at the order's own price has risen since t by at least divisor x (queue + stake), so GBP 2 needs a rise of 4 at the front and 2 x (queue + 2) behind a queue. One fill, in full, at the order's own price. Nothing published at or before t fills. No fill is credited from a batch that is not open (data.traded_volume.rule). Once inPlay was true before a batch, a lapse order is no longer judged. So the batch that itself turns the market in play is still judged, on the ladder as that batch leaves it; its fills are counted apart (diagnostics.rule). The cross test needs the stake only, where lp-v1 needed queue + stake: by price-time priority an opposing order can come to rest at or through our price only after every order ahead of ours there is matched or pulled, so asking for the queue again would count it twice. Inference, not checked on real files. Over a window of hours: the queue is fixed at t and is never lowered for size cancelled ahead of the order, so the central and pessimistic models miss the fills a real order would get after such cancellations, more so the longer the order rests, and the fills they keep lean towards the adverse ones. Size that joins the price later is never put ahead of the order. The order keeps its price when the best price moves away. The rule files ask for size shown at the order's price at t, so the optimistic model is a bound, not a place the order can start from. Rises in the after-the-hour seconds are not counted (data.traded_volume.rule).

grid.rule: A cell is one rule file at one of its times: two rule files x four times = 8 cells. Placed at off - 14400 s, off - 7200 s, off - 3600 s or off - 1800 s and pulled at off - 600 s; t = the first-published scheduled marketTime + at_s. Each cell is an independent hypothetical: its orders are our only orders in the market. A favourite cell holds one order a market. A cell of the each_active file holds one order on each runner that passes the runner rows, each judged alone. The view at t holds every message published at or before t; an order rests from that batch with no delay, through every message published after t up to and including the pull time. It is never re-priced. A lapse order also ends when the market turns in play before its pull time.

bsp_ends.rule: The stream appears to cut BSP to two decimals (docs/data-audit.md: a 2017 sample, unchecked on 2015-16), so the true BSP lies between the value as written and that plus step. Every g and net is computed twice: against BSP as written and against BSP + step. The kill end is the figure that favours the order (LAY: BSP + step; BACK: as written); the claim end is the other. If at least whole_hundredths_share of the scored orders' BSPs are whole hundredths, kills read the kill end and claims the claim end; else the as-written figure decides alone. The share is taken once per pass, over every scored order of both labels. names lists the two ends, as written first. Both are printed either way. BSP is never snapped to a tick.

bsp_valid_if: the market's final status is CLOSED and its last bspReconciled is true
the runner is listed at the end with final status WINNER or LOSER
its final bsp is a finite number above 1 (the index keeps none below 1.01)
measurement.classes_rule: Every order rulefile.decide returns is a placed order and ends in exactly one class, the first that applies, from facts that do not depend on a fill. The first five are movement-v1's (movement.measure), for the selected runner and the runners ACTIVE and listed at t: outcome_unknown when the member was not read whole or a runner's later state cannot be assessed; void_own_runner_removed when the selected runner was removed after t; post_decision_removal when another of those runners was; result_revised_after_close; missing_bsp when bsp_valid_if fails. Then stream_malformed_after_placement when a ladder entry, a trd entry or an rc runner id published after t and up to the pull time could not be read. Else scored. A suspension, an early off or a revised schedule after t does not drop an order: the fill rules handle them and the tables count them. Only scored orders enter a statistic; every other class stays in the placed counts with its fill counts per model. Market-level void cannot be seen in these files and is never inferred.
measurement.commission_source: Yu, 2026-11-11: the account is on Basic 2%
measurement.deciding_net: The closing lines read net_closed over the pessimistic model's filled orders (verdicts.rule). This departs from close-v1, whose kill read the optimistic model and whose claim read net_held. net_closed is read because only a LAY is asked, and a LAY is closed with a BACK: close-v1's registration says a GBP 2 BACK cannot be closed at BSP, because a BSP lay has a GBP 10 minimum liability (fact F38), so for a BACK net_closed is a bound no real order reaches. Fact F38 gives a GBP 1 minimum bet; whether a BACK of this size is taken at BSP is not checked here, and the closing order is not simulated. net_held is printed beside net_closed and decides nothing.
measurement.g: Per GBP 1 of backer's stake, positive is good for the order: a BACK at P scores g = P / BSP - 1 and a LAY at L scores g = 1 - L / BSP. Every placed order has a g at its own price, filled or not.
measurement.intent_to_treat: Per cell and partition label, over scored orders: (1) the mean over filled orders, per model, of g, net_closed and net_held; (2) the mean g over all placed orders, each valued at its own price, filled or not, with no fill model; (3) the value per placed order, net_held when filled and 0 when not, per model; (4) the gap, mean g over filled minus mean g over unfilled, per model, as a CR1 contrast by race date. The value per placed order is given only when that model's filled figures are. The gap is given when the filled and the unfilled orders each number statistics.min_values, with an interval from uncertainty.min_clusters race dates and no p-value.
measurement.mid: the mid at t is (best back + best lay) / 2 of the order's runner at t when its best back is below its best lay and they are at most null.max_spread_ticks CLASSIC ticks apart; the explore pass prints it against BSP beside the placed mean, valued as g is with the mid in place of the order's price. Neither the placed mean nor the mid is a fill figure: across a wide gap both look good by construction, and no closing line reads them.
measurement.net_closed: g - commission_rate x max(g, 0), unrounded: the order closed at BSP at equal stakes. It is the kinder net, always at or above net_held.
measurement.net_held: the order held to the result, unrounded: for a BACK g - commission_rate x (P - 1) / BSP (contract p1's NCLV); for a LAY g - commission_rate x (1 - 1 / BSP).
measurement.part_and_rest: A mean, SD, range or interval for a part of a group is given only if the part and the rest each hold statistics.min_values values. If a model's unfilled part is smaller, that model's filled figures in the explore pass are replaced by the all-placed figures and flagged filled_is_all_placed; in the blind look that model's SD and ranges are not given at all (blind_pass.withholds). A size gate always counts the model's own fills and their race dates. The rule is applied to each group it is asked of: a cell on the explore label, or a half-year of it. Across a split it is applied whole, in the explore pass's tables; a figure held back keeps its counts and shows rest_not_given. (1) Across the fill models. The three models' fills lie inside one another, so two filled means over groups a few orders apart would give those few orders' mean. In one group of orders the models are taken in the order pessimistic, optimistic, central. The group's orders are sorted into classes, two orders being in one class when every figure given so far, and the one now asked, is taken over both of them or over neither. A model's filled figures, its value per placed order and its gap are given only if every class then holds statistics.min_values orders. (2) Across half-years. A half-year's figure is given only when the other half-year gives that figure too, and a model's figures only when both half-years take them over the same kind of group (the same filled_is_all_placed flag). Nothing is selected or labelled by the code, nothing is pooled over two labels and no null mean is given, so close-v1's rules for those cases have nothing to act on. Not covered: the blind look gives one SD per model, and two SDs over groups a few orders apart can bound how far those orders lie from the mean, not on which side; the explore pass gives each group's own mean and SD beside them. This is a known residual release.
measurement.removals: No re-pricing. An order whose own runner is removed after t is classed void_own_runner_removed, and one with any other runner removed after t, even after the pull time, is classed post_decision_removal; neither is scored. An order that rests for hours meets more removals than one that rests for minutes, and a live order cannot leave those races out: the scored orders are picked by a later event nobody knows at t. Live, a removal can cut matched prices and cancel unmatched lays; neither is modelled, and docs/betfair-facts.md has no reduction-factor entry. The lean this leaves is unmeasured in size and in sign. The size of each class is printed per cell (B3), with its fills (B4), and again beside each cell's figures (E1); every closing word is reported with the share of orders not scored.
measurement.unit: a fraction of the backer's stake; tables print 100 x g as points of stake. These are not lp-v1's implied-probability points, which are differences of 100 / price.

not_measured: latency: the orders rest from the batch at t with no delay
queue position: no tier shows it, so three fill models stand in for it, and over hours the size shown at t says less and less about it
cancellations ahead of the order, which no model credits (fill_models.rule)
partial fills: every fill is all or nothing, a trade through the price included
virtual (cross-matched) prices, which the files' ladders exclude
removals: classed, never re-priced by a reduction factor
the closing order: its minimum size, its rounding, and whether an equal-stake close averages like an exact one
any effect of our own order on a thin early book

null.label: close-v1/null/{market_id}/{at_s}/{rule_id}
null.rule: Not read in this study. A time u is still drawn for every order because the walk is close-v1's, with one draw per market and cell, so the orders of one each_active cell in one market share their u. B7 counts the null values by reason; no figure of a null value is given by either pass. The other fields of this block keep close-v1's values because the parser fixes them; max_spread_ticks is also the cap the mid uses (measurement.mid).

population.codes_rule: Per cell, every index record gets exactly one code, the first that applies in this order, or issued. Codes reconcile to the record count per cell. The first twelve are movement-v1's history gates and market predicates (movement.market_code), read against the rule file's market block from what was published at or before t; anchor_not_known_by_decision says the off time was first published after t, so the file starts too late for that cell. Then partition_not_registered (data.partitions): here, every record that is not on the explore label. Then bsp_market_false when the rule file gates bsp_market and bspMarket as of t is exactly false; a missing value passes and is counted (diagnostics). A record whose cells all have a code by now is never opened. Then ladder_malformed. Then the code rulefile.decide gives for the view at t, in its order: the rule file's market rows (market_not_open, too_few_active_runners); the selector's codes (no_priced_active_runner and favourite_tie for the favourite file, no_active_runner for the each_active file); the runner rows (no_best_back in the each_active file, then best_back_out_of_range, depth_below_min, no_best_lay, gap_not_1_to_20_ticks) and no_reference_price. A feature with no value fails its row, so no_best_back and no_best_lay count the runners with no quote on that side, and gap_not_1_to_20_ticks covers a crossed or locked book, a price off the CLASSIC ladder and a gap above 20 ticks. For a cell of the each_active file the code is a market's: issued when at least one runner got an order; when none did, the code rulefile.decide gives, which is the first runner's. B8 gives every runner's own code. Then price_off_ladder: an order whose price is not a CLASSIC ladder price is not placed, and this is the cell's code only when no order is left. A when row of a rule file may not use one of the harness's own codes, and every when code must be in this list.
population.price_ladder: CLASSIC assumed for GB and IE horse-racing WIN markets, as movement-v1 and lp-v1 assume: index v1 does not track priceLadderDefinition, so every order price is checked against the CLASSIC ladder instead
population.quotes: PRO's atb and atl, folded as movement-v1 folds them (movement.LadderFold): price-keyed [price, size] deltas, where a size of 0 deletes that price and an empty list empties that ladder; a null value changes nothing; an image (img true) replaces every runner's ladders. A runner's best back is the highest price of its back ladder and its best lay the lowest of its lay ladder, each with its size, as the file wrote them. The view a rule file reads (resting.view_of) holds the runners ACTIVE and listed at t, each with its best back, the size there, its best lay and the CLASSIC ticks between them; market_open is 1 when the status as of t is OPEN and inPlay as of t is not true. Quotes are not cleared while the market is not OPEN: the rule files' market_open row refuses a decision then, and no fill is credited from a batch that is not open.
population.source: the two rule files (data.rules): close-v1's LAY file with four earlier times, a row for a missing best lay and a gap gate of 1 to 20 ticks, on the favourite and, in a second price range, on each active runner; not a pilot contract

releases: There is no registered pass: the runner refuses it for this study id. The key is kept because the parser fixes its name. The explore pass gives everything the blind look gives, number for number, and adds, on the explore label only, each headed exploratory with its number of cells c and sqrt(2 ln c):
E1: per cell, at both BSP ends: the figures of measurement.intent_to_treat with n, race dates, SD and CR1 95% interval; the mid at t against BSP; the size of each class that is not scored
E3: the quantiles of the sum of 1 / BSP per market with a scored order
registered_pass.rule: Nothing is tested, bounded, selected or labelled by the code. A group below statistics.min_values gives counts only. A cell below the gate of statistics.rule gives counts only in E1 and E2. Of PRO-V the explore pass gives index record counts and nothing else. No outcome figure is given by gap, or by price within a cell; the table by gap (B9) gives counts only.

selection.rule: Not used: nothing is selected. The other fields of this block keep close-v1's values because the parser asks for them.

statistics.rule: A group with fewer than min_values values gives counts only, in either pass: no SD, quantile, range, mean or interval. In the explore pass a cell gives figures only when the pessimistic model has min_tested_values fills on min_tested_race_dates race dates; else counts only. Nothing is tested, bounded or selected and no p-value is printed in either pass; every interval is descriptive, and each of the explore pass's tables E1, E2 and E3 prints its number of cells c and sqrt(2 ln c). Intervals are CR1 by race date (uncertainty.rule). Quantiles are by nearest rank: with n sorted values, the q quantile is value ceil(q x n), counted from 1. The blind look gives the quantiles of an outcome only as the symmetric ranges q(1 - a) - q(a), so quantiles must hold 1 - a beside every a. Floats are rounded to 6 places, quantiles and ranges to 4. The SD is the sample SD, with n - 1. No detectable effect is printed: it describes a test, and none is run; detectable_level and power keep close-v1's values because the parser asks for them.

summary: Registered offline measurement on the explore dates only; not a backtest contract and not a test. It asks whether a resting GBP 2 LAY at the best back price, placed 4 hours, 2 hours, 1 hour or 30 minutes before the off and pulled 10 minutes before it, is filled at a price that beats BSP once the order is closed there. Two frozen rule files say what is ordered (data.rules): one order on the favourite priced 1.50 to 4.00, and one order on each runner priced 4.00 to 10.00, on GB and IE horse-racing WIN markets rebuilt from the free 2015-05..2016-04 Betfair Historical Data PRO files. Only a LAY is asked, because at this stake a BACK cannot be closed at BSP (measurement.deciding_net). An order here is a simulated intent; nothing can reach an exchange. Every order is judged under close-v1's three fill models, with one change: a rise of traded volume in the first seconds after a whole hour is not counted (data.traded_volume). Both passes read PRO-D alone and open no file of a PRO-V date (data.partitions). A blind look gives counts and spreads only. One explore pass, on a later night, adds the means. Nothing is tested and no alpha is spent. The closing lines are in verdicts.rule and were written before any pass. A cell can be ended here; none can be confirmed.

uncertainty.rule: As movement-v1 and lp-v1: m = sum(x) / N, SE^2 = G / (G - 1) x the sum over race dates g of (the sum over values i in g of (x_i - m))^2 / N^2, and the interval m +/- t x SE with t the (1 + confidence_level) / 2 quantile of Student's t with G - 1 degrees of freedom; fewer than min_clusters race dates give the mean without an interval. The race date is the Europe/London calendar date of the first-published off. The four times of one market, both rule files and the several runners of one race share a race date, so their dependence stays inside one cluster.

verdicts.prediction: (1) The four cells at 30 minutes and at 1 hour pass the stop rules; a 4-hour cell is dropped with about four chances in ten. (2) No cell reads "kept as a lead"; about one chance in eight that one does. (3) At most two cells read "ended", most likely none or one; every other cell that is read is "unclear". (4) In every cell that prints a gap, the filled orders score below the unfilled ones.
verdicts.printed_with: PRO 2015-16, explore dates only: a kill gate and a prior, never confirmation. Every fill is simulated.
verdicts.rule: No label is issued by the code; names and the levels are kept because the parser asks, and nothing reads them. lab-Claude reads one word per cell from the explore pass's summary.json, the first that applies. The figure is the pessimistic model's filled net_closed on the explore label, with its CR1 95% interval. (1) dropped: a stop rule of blind_pass.rule fired for the cell. (2) not given: the figure is not given at bsp_plus_step or at bsp_as_written. (3) ended: at bsp_plus_step, the kill end, the interval's upper end is below 0; a figure flagged filled_is_all_placed may read ended. (4) kept as a lead: the figure is not flagged filled_is_all_placed; at bsp_as_written, the claim end, the interval's lower end is above 0; and its means in H1 and in H2 are both given and above 0, each on half_year_min_fills or more pessimistic fills. (5) unclear. A mean alone never ends a cell and never makes a lead. If the switch of measurement.bsp_ends says the two ends do not decide apart, the as-written figure is read wherever an end is named. Nothing else enters a word: not another model, not net_held, not the placed mean, not the mid, not the gap at t, not another cell. This departs from close-v1 twice, on purpose: ended reads the pessimistic model where close-v1's kill read the optimistic one, and a lead reads net_closed where close-v1's claim read net_held (measurement.deciding_net). The pessimistic model leans against the order more the longer it rests (fill_models.rule), so ended means ended for an order at the back of the queue, and every word is reported with the optimistic and central figures beside it where they are given, the fill rate and the share of orders not scored. Ended or dropped closes that cell; when every cell of a rule file is ended or dropped, that rule file's early variant is closed. A lead is reported to Yu and starts nothing: what a lead may earn is Yu's to say. Unclear and not given start nothing. No word leads to a live rule, a money number, a policy page, a second explore pass or a result in Git.
